neighbours.label: the noun that completes 'the human ___' (eye, brain, hand, body, ear); the same nouns without 'human' stay quiet
fire: The lens can resolve details far smaller than the human eye can.
Nothing built so far is as flexible as the human hand.
Sleep clears waste from the human brain every night.
Sounds above that pitch are too high for the human ear to catch.
About sixty percent of the human body is water.
The valve works much like the one in the human heart.
The flute comes closest to the sound of the human voice.
These tools were shaped to fit the human hand long before metal was known.
quiet: The lens can resolve details far smaller than a grain of sand.
Nothing built so far is as flexible as a willow branch.
Rain clears dust from the city streets every night.
Sounds above that pitch are too high for the old radio to catch.
About sixty percent of the lake is covered with ice.
The valve works much like the one in a bicycle pump.
The owl turned its left eye toward the lamp and blinked.
The surgeon stitched the cut on his hand in ten minutes.

notes: Probes: 'the human eye' 0.67 and 0.56, 'the human hand' 0.47, 'the human brain' 0.42; but also 'we cannot see' 0.58, 'what is perceived' 0.41, 'first airplane' 0.39, 'first telephone' 0.30, 'beyond the mind' 0.30, so this frame is one of several things the pole does; 'Come and see' 0.01, a red bicycle 0.05.
